A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FINC study despite changes to the title and format. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original controlled clustering experiments, generative-model comparisons, runtime measurements in Table 1, and additional image/video analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds experiments identifying high-memorization and high/low text-image alignment clusters.

M1.justification: FINC's Fourier features, covariance difference, and eigendecomposition procedure remain unchanged. The similarity score added to Algorithm 1 already appeared in v2 Section 5.2; the new applications reuse FINC on score-selected sample groups.

E1.justification: Sections 5.3–5.4 add two diagnostic tasks: identifying sample types associated with memorization on ImageNet and text-image alignment on MS-COCO. Existing image, video, and text-to-image coverage is retained; the expansion concerns task requirements rather than new datasets.

E2.justification: Table 1 and corresponding qualitative comparisons retain Rarity plus spectral clustering, FLD plus spectral clustering, and KEN with its existing decomposition variants. SD-XL and Kandinsky are generators examined in the new alignment study, not additional methods evaluated against FINC.

E3.justification: The new studies introduce comparisons between the top 20% and bottom 20% of generated samples ranked by FLD memorization score or CLIPScore. These use ImageNet training data for memorization and MS-COCO prompts for alignment, including newly evaluated SD-XL and Kandinsky. Existing sample budgets, Fourier-feature selection, and runtime protocols are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds diagnostic analyses of category-dependent memorization and alignment, including similar training images for high-FLD clusters in Figure 11 and high/low CLIPScore examples in Figure 15. Earlier bandwidth sensitivity, feature-extractor comparisons, and unseen-sample scoring analyses remain.

E5.justification: The mode-frequency estimates with plus/minus quantities in v2 Figure 19 are retained in v3 Figure 22. No new empirical run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds high-FLD cluster results for five generators and top/bottom CLIPScore clusters for GigaGAN, SD-XL, and Kandinsky. For example, Figure 15 shows zebras in the leading high-CLIPScore mode for all three models. Table 1 runtimes and the earlier qualitative and mode-frequency results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 replaces the Gaussian sampling assumption with sampling from the Fourier transform of a normalized shift-invariant kernel, broadening its stated scope. The approximation bounds are unchanged, and Appendix A retains the Gaussian-specific derivation rather than supplying a generalized proof.

C1.justification: The central FINC and scalability contributions remain, but the introduction adds memorization/alignment applications and explicitly claims novelty for the non-Hermitian perturbation analysis. It also changes logarithmic feature-size growth to 'sub-logarithmic,' despite retaining the logarithmic bound.

C2.justification: Appendix B.5 newly interprets differences between high/low CLIPScore categories as differences in alignment performance. Meanwhile, v2's explicit limitation that weaker embeddings may impair FINC on non-vision data is removed. Existing bandwidth and feature-extractor interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 documents data-processing steps for the new diagnostics, including score-based percentile selection, eigenvector-ranked representative images, and retrieval of similar training examples. Existing bandwidth selection, Fourier-feature grid, PyTorch/hardware information, and code-access disclosure remain, with several details relocated to Appendix B.1.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations and discussion concerning asymmetric-kernel Fourier features, CLIPScore, and scalable or online generative-model evaluation. Section 2 also changes the single-cell RNA discussion from a similar clustering task to an explicitly distinct biological task, while retaining the central positioning against KEN and sample-based novelty scores.

P1.justification: v3 changes the title and affiliations, rewrites selected introductory and related-work passages, condenses preliminaries and settings, and reorganizes experimental subsections and Appendix B. The overall section sequence and most existing explanatory text remain.

P2.justification: The main paper and references change from one-column to two-column layout, with extensive resizing and rearrangement of figures and tables. Fashion-MNIST moves to the appendix, and new memorization and alignment displays appear. The LDM caption changes from top-3 to top-2 to match the existing two-mode display.

improvement.justification: The new diagnostic studies make FINC's practical use more concrete, particularly the generated-to-training-image comparisons in Figure 11 and prompt-associated alignment examples in Figure 15. These provide a modest empirical benefit beyond v2's frequency comparisons. The gain is limited by removal of the embedding limitation, retention of a Gaussian-specific proof under broader theorem assumptions, and the new 'sub-logarithmic' wording conflicting with the displayed bound.
